newsitem.title: USA: South Carolina executes triple murderer.
newsitem.headline: South Carolina executes triple murderer.

text.p: - A South Carolina man who said he had no remorse for killing two millworkers and a prostitute, was executed by lethal injection early on Friday, prison officials said.
Michael Torrence was the third person executed in South Carolina this year and the fourth to die by lethal injection since the state began offering that option in July 1995.
South Carolina has executed 249 people since 1912 including eight since 1985 after the state restored the death penalty in 1977.
The execution took place at Columbia's Broad River Correctional Institution at 1:21 a.m. (0521 GMT), prisons spokesman John Barkley said.
He ate a last meal of steak, shrimp and lobster prepared by a Japanese restaurant and wanted to make his body available for medical research.

Torrence, 35, was convicted in the February 1987 deaths of Dennis Lollis and Charles Bush during a robbery. A month later, he shot Charleston prostitute Cynthia Williams and dumped her body along a highway.
Torrence, a sixth-grade dropout who had been on Death Row for eight years, wanted to die and had petitioned the South Carolina Supreme Court since 1994 to let him drop his appeals.
"When I committed these crimes, I knew what I was doing," he told the court two years ago. "I just don't see where spending 20 or 30 more years here is gonna benefit me."
Just before the execution, Torrence said in a brief statement read by his lawyer that he "understands an apology is not sufficient, but hopes his understanding gives them some comfort."
The Fourth U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals on Thursday night denied a lawyer's request to stop the execution, and the U.S. Supreme Court was not asked to rule.
South Carolina Gov. David Beasley on Thursday also declined to grant clemency to Torrence.

About 20 protesters gathered outside the Governor's Mansion ahead of the execution, but were unable to light their candles for a service and vigil because of winds spawned by Hurricane Fran, which had just reached landfall in North Carolina.
